title: 0sfs · repository split
summary: Flight repositories and their upstream shared dependencies.
ownershipNote: The flight application consumes FOSS Earth. Shared globe, viewer and tooling packages do not depend back on the flight application. Content and tooling relations are distinct from runtime imports.

groups.title: Flight application & publication
groups.note: Flight composition, branding and pinned releases.

groups.title: Flight feature repositories
groups.note: One feature tab normally identifies its repository.

groups.title: Engine families
groups.note: Definitions, geometry and optional source profiles.

groups.title: FOSS Earth dependencies
groups.note: Shared owners; no dependency back into flight.

groups.title: App-owned data & device/native owners
groups.note: Manifests are data; dynamics and controller handling retain their owners.

groups.title: Flight docs, research & tools
groups.note: Flight-specific wrappers consume generic FOSS Earth tooling.

nodes.name: 0sfs/simulator
nodes.detail: Flight composition, accepted fixed steps, JSBSim adapters, flight cameras, saved-flight lifecycle and final control application.
nodes.note: The host advances physics and writes the final control command once. Feature packages return observations, intents and status.

nodes.name: 0sfs/0sfs.github.io
nodes.detail: Public website and deployment of an explicitly pinned simulator release; no second copy of simulator source.

nodes.name: 0sfs/dev
nodes.detail: Flight-owned developer/debug panels, accepted-step inspection and flight contribution metadata. Uses the shared FOSS Earth Dev framework.
nodes.note: The shared ?dev=1 switch activates registered flight contributions. FOSS Earth does not import this package.

nodes.name: 0sfs/logo
nodes.detail: Flight logo generators, source assets, licenses and exported logo artifacts. It does not own FOSS Earth or UMN branding.

nodes.name: 0sfs/aircraft
nodes.detail: Shared manifest/schema, catalog and loading contracts, aircraft visual installation and selection panel.

nodes.name: 0sfs/fuel
nodes.detail: Fuel panel, read/write/distribution interfaces and external-tank installation. Native fuel and mass dynamics remain in JSBSim.

nodes.name: 0sfs/autopilot
nodes.detail: Hold controller, engagement, modes, pilot takeover, backend contracts, parameter definitions and panel.
nodes.note: Returns control intents to the host. It does not import the simulator, write final controls or absorb aircraft-specific fly-by-wire laws.

nodes.name: 0sfs/controls
nodes.detail: Flight action mapping, keyboard response, assists, flight haptic interpretation and panel contributions. Device handling remains in gamepad-tools.

nodes.name: 0sfs/remote-control
nodes.detail: Phone app, pairing, transport/protocol, control sharing, phone settings and camera transport/playout through host adapters.

nodes.name: 0sfs/sound
nodes.detail: Shared audio runtime, DSP/WASM/worklet host, mixing, propagation, resource limits, Sound panel and pure source-plugin contracts. The application registers source plugins.
nodes.note: The sound runtime does not statically import engine-sound or wind-noise. Plugin implementations consume pure Sound contracts; the host supplies observations and installs plugins.

nodes.name: 0sfs/exhaust
nodes.detail: Gas optics, plume and smoke rendering, plume depth handling, hot-surface rendering and Exhaust panel.
nodes.note: Native combustion/thermal state comes through accepted observations. Engine optics are content; mechanical geometry/nozzle articulation remain with engine packages and installations.

nodes.name: 0sfs/engines
nodes.detail: Common engine contracts, family registration/loading, observations, monitor/instruments, live history and test-stand interface. Family packages register through pure core/schema exports; native algorithms stay in JSBSim.
nodes.note: Common engines accepts installed family registrations. It does not statically import F135, FJ33 or IO320 implementations; optional panel entry points consume the shared interface.

nodes.name: 0sfs/g-forces
nodes.detail: Pilot-load interpretation, meter, blackout/redout/consciousness behavior, overlays and panel. Reports pilot availability to host control integration.

nodes.name: 0sfs/logging
nodes.detail: Flight data recorder, channels, bounded history, segments/marks, export and Logging panel. Records accepted state and applied controls; the status log belongs to interface.

nodes.name: 0sfs/ground-contact
nodes.detail: Aircraft/world contact adaptation, collision queries and response integration. Terrain support queries remain FOSS Earth's; native contact-force laws remain JSBSim's.
nodes.note: A documented tab exception. No second authoritative friction solver or independent physics loop is introduced.

nodes.name: 0sfs/about
nodes.detail: Flight-specific About composition, branding and release/dependency manifest content. Consumes the generic FOSS Earth viewer without copying it.
nodes.note: The flight manifest is owned here or supplied by the simulator build. It is never the data source of the standalone globe or campus tour.

nodes.name: 0sfs/F-35B
nodes.detail: F-35B flight model/systems, assets, powered-lift installation, rigging, fuel/contact geometry, control-law configuration and validation.

nodes.name: 0sfs/SF-50
nodes.detail: SF50 models/generations, systems, assets, FJ33 installation, fuel/contact geometry and validation.

nodes.name: 0sfs/C172
nodes.detail: Current C172P package, propeller and engine references, systems, geometry and validation. Engine identity follows the installed eng_io320.xml.

nodes.name: 0sfs/F135
nodes.detail: F135-specific native definitions/calibration, geometry, installation contracts, acoustic source data, optical tables, provenance and evidence.

nodes.name: 0sfs/FJ33
nodes.detail: FJ33 family definitions and supported variants, geometry, optional acoustic/optical capabilities, provenance and validation. A future FJ44 is a separate family.

nodes.name: 0sfs/IO320
nodes.detail: Package identity follows the current eng_io320.xml. Preserves definition provenance; future acoustic/optical capabilities must be stated explicitly.

nodes.name: foss-earth/engine
nodes.detail: Proposed shared globe-engine extraction: terrain, imagery, coordinates, authoritative surface queries, globe camera/input and world integration. It consumes the shared renderer for scene/device/frame services.
nodes.note: Globe code owns maps and surface queries. Renderer owns device, scene, backends and frame scheduling; its API has no import back into the globe engine.

nodes.name: foss-earth/ui
nodes.detail: Generic windows/tabs, settings registry/types/widgets, contribution registration, status log and report contracts. Each host registers its own feature catalogs and callbacks.
nodes.note: UI imports neither globe/renderer implementations nor flight/campus packages. Toolbar and feature panels consume its primitives. Shared ?dev=1 plumbing activates only host-registered developer contributions.

nodes.name: foss-earth/about
nodes.detail: Shared build identity/provenance and dependency graph viewer. Reads a host-supplied manifest without importing any described runtime.
nodes.note: Viewer code belongs to FOSS Earth; application-branded data, release pins and graph content belong to each application.

nodes.name: foss-earth/sky
nodes.detail: Shared astronomy, clear atmosphere, stars, physical lighting and optional renderer/panels.
nodes.note: Terrain-lighting, settings and scene-time ports are supplied by the host. No import back into globe engine and no flight dependency.

nodes.name: foss-earth/weather
nodes.detail: Canonical world weather definition, sampling, sources, optional rendering and shared panel. Aircraft samples and visuals consume one field.
nodes.note: The larger weather model is a specification, not a completed extraction. Core imports neither globe runtime nor JSBSim.

nodes.name: foss-earth/panorama
nodes.detail: Generic scene schema, loader, panorama viewer, image preparation and validation tools. Campus photographs and placements remain UMN-owned.

nodes.name: foss-earth/dev
nodes.detail: Shared developer-tab plumbing, graph/debug widget services and the ?dev=1 activation contract. Hosts register distinct app-owned developer panels.
nodes.note: This framework does not import simulator debug code or a particular tour. Enabling Dev does not create another physics loop.

nodes.name: foss-earth/dev_installer
nodes.detail: Generic setup/update/doctor machinery that reads an explicit versioned workspace manifest. It does not hardcode downstream projects or import their runtime packages.

nodes.name: foss-earth/ci
nodes.detail: Shared reviewed workflows, checks and authorship validator machinery. Each consumer owns a thin pinned workflow entry point and its component-specific tests.
nodes.note: Tooling reuse is not a runtime dependency. The shared validator does not own app-specific build or qualification claims.

nodes.name: 0sfs release manifest
nodes.detail: The one flight release/dependency manifest describing installed code/content versions, revisions, licensing and typed relations. Data contract, not a repository.

nodes.name: 0sfs workspace manifest
nodes.detail: Flight checkouts, compatible revisions, toolchains and build order for the generic setup CLI. Data contract, not a repository.

nodes.name: Felipegalind0/jsbsim
nodes.detail: Owned maintained checkout of upstream JSBSim: flight dynamics, native contact/atmosphere/engine work and the verified WASM SDK artifact.
nodes.note: Shared CI adoption, if used, applies to this owned fork. Upstream JSBSim retains its own governance and contribution path.

nodes.name: Felipegalind0/gamepad-tools
nodes.detail: Controller handling and bindings shared by globe and flight. Flight interpretation remains in controls.

nodes.name: 0sfs/docs
nodes.detail: Published architecture/ownership map, integration guides, cross-project specifications and release compatibility docs. Assembles or links versioned component docs.

nodes.name: 0sfs/research
nodes.detail: Research questions, sources, alternative approaches, experiments and reproducible methods across aircraft/engines. Findings do not qualify a release automatically.

nodes.name: 0sfs/.github
nodes.detail: Community contribution documents, policy guidance and repository templates. Executable shared checks and authorship validators belong to 0sfs/ci.
nodes.note: Default organization documentation alone does not enforce a merge check. Each repository explicitly installs the pinned CI entry point.

nodes.name: 0sfs/ci
nodes.detail: Flight-specific shared workflow composition and test/build orchestration. Consumes generic FOSS Earth CI/authorship machinery; Earth and UMN do not call it.

nodes.name: 0sfs/dev_installer
nodes.detail: Flight setup/update/doctor entry point and workspace selection. Consumes the generic FOSS Earth installer using the flight-owned manifest.

nodes.name: foss-earth/renderer
nodes.detail: Shared device/scene lifecycle, WebGPU/WebGL backends, readiness, frame scheduler and optional Renderer panel.
nodes.note: Renderer never imports the globe engine. Its optional panel consumes UI; map and aircraft contributions arrive through explicit services.

nodes.name: foss-earth/toolbar
nodes.detail: Bottom HUD layout and display of registered callbacks/values. Hosts supply map, position, renderer, input and app-specific items through public contracts.
nodes.note: Consumes generic UI primitives. It does not import the implementations whose values/buttons it shows; each setting still has one tab home.

nodes.name: 0sfs/engine-sound
nodes.detail: Engine acoustic source plugin consuming accepted engine observations and optional installed family profiles. Registered by the flight host through pure Sound contracts.
nodes.note: Optional profile capabilities remain proposed. Common sound runtime has no code import of this plugin; native engine physics remains in JSBSim.

nodes.name: 0sfs/wind-noise
nodes.detail: Airframe/airflow acoustic source plugin. Receives accepted airflow and airframe observations from the host and consumes pure Sound plugin contracts.
nodes.note: It imports no weather world or sampler. The host supplies the relevant observations; the plugin creates no independent world or physics loop.
